outcome: Read a range of 19th, 20th and 21st century literature, literary non-fiction, reviews and journalism with understanding.
Identify and interpret themes, ideas and information, reading in different ways for different purposes.
Compare and evaluate how useful, relevant and well presented content is for a given purpose.
Draw inferences and back them with evidence from the text to support a point of view.
Spot bias and misuse of evidence, separating supported statements from unsupported ones.
Reflect critically on a text using its context and wider reading, recognising that responses can differ.
Identify main themes and summarise ideas and information from a single text.
Synthesise information from more than one text.
Explain how a writer's vocabulary and grammar create effect, using accurate linguistic and literary terms.
Analyse and evaluate how form and structure add to a text's impact.
Compare two or more texts critically on all these points.
Write to describe, narrate, explain, instruct, inform, respond and argue for different audiences and purposes.
Choose vocabulary, grammar, form and structure to suit audience, purpose and context.
Use language imaginatively and creatively and use information from others to write in different forms.
Keep a consistent point of view and coherence across a whole text.
Select, organise and emphasise facts, ideas and key points, citing evidence and quotation pertinently.
Create emotional impact and write persuasively using rhetorical devices such as rhetorical questions, antithesis and parenthesis.
Use Standard English, correct grammar, punctuation and spelling with a wide vocabulary and grammatical terminology.
Select and organise information and ideas effectively and persuasively for prepared spoken presentations and speeches.
Plan a presentation for different purposes and audiences.
Listen and respond appropriately to questions and feedback.
Express ideas in spoken Standard English whenever appropriate.
